problem: The claim 'The eye does not need to change focus when it moves from the instrument panel to the HUD' is wrong. Collimated symbols are at infinity, while the instrument panel is a near object (roughly 0.5 m). Moving the gaze from the panel to the HUD does need a change of accommodation. The real benefit of collimation is that the symbols and the distant outside scene are at the same focus, so the pilot does not refocus between the symbols and the runway.
fix: 'Because the rays are parallel, the symbols appear focused at infinity, the same distance as the outside scene. The pilot can read the symbols and watch the runway without changing focus. A screen sits at a short distance and forces the eye to refocus every time the pilot looks from the screen to the outside world.' (Do not claim that no refocus is needed between the near panel and the HUD.)

where: Section 1, formula definition and Worked example 1
problem: θ is defined as the 'look-down angle' from the eye to the combiner, but h is defined as the height of the combiner above the eye. If the combiner is above the eye line, the eye looks up, not down. The name and the geometry contradict each other, and Worked example 1 (75 mm above the eye) is really an angle of elevation.
fix: Define θ as 'the angle of the combiner above the pilot's forward line of sight (an elevation angle)'. Then tan θ = h / d with h = height of the combiner above the eye line and d = forward distance from the eye to the combiner. Change the answer line of Worked example 1 to 'The combiner is θ ≈ 8.5° above the forward line of sight.' If a true look-down angle is wanted, put the combiner below the eye line and say so.

where: Figure (HUD and HMD light path) and its caption
problem: The dashed edge p → h shows light going from the HUD projector to the helmet display, which is not physical: an HMD has its own display and optics. The caption 'both paths end at the same eye' also suggests a HUD and an HMD are used at the same time on the same eye, which is normally not the case.
fix: Draw the dashed edge from 'Symbol generator' (s) to 'Helmet display' (h), keep h → e, and caption it: 'The HUD path and the helmet-display path may share the symbol generator; a HUD and an HMD are alternatives, not usually viewed together.'

problem: 'The eye relief and exit pupil must allow the pilot to see the whole symbol' is unclear: there is no single 'symbol' to see; eye relief and exit pupil decide whether the pilot sees the whole image (full field of view) without vignetting.
fix: 'The eye relief and exit pupil must be large enough for the pilot to see the whole displayed image, even with the helmet moving slightly on the head.'

problem: The answer says the eyes 'do not need to refocus', which repeats the error in Section 1 and suggests no accommodation change at all when moving from the panel to the HUD.
fix: 'The pilot reads the symbols while looking forward at the outside scene, so the eyes stay on the forward view instead of moving down to the panel. The symbols and the outside scene are both at infinity, so the pilot also avoids refocusing between them.'
